claims.statement: All MD3 numeric values (shape, motion, state, typescale, colour roles) are authoritative only when taken from the material-web v0.192 generated token source files under tokens/versions/v0_192/; m3.material.io is illustrative only because it is JS-rendered and cannot be fetched, and on any conflict the upstream token file wins over memory or second-hand summaries.

The upstream material-web token files are deliberately not vendored into this repository, so every 'matches material-web v0.192' assertion is a human source-verified claim rather than a machine-comparable equation; md3ConfigTokens.test.ts compares tokens.css and tailwind.config.ts against expected values copied into the test, so a value that was copied wrong upstream and mirrored in the test stays green.

styles/tokens.css is the single source of truth for every --md-* value and tailwind.config.ts's colors object may only hold var(--md-*) references (no literals), with the Fluent-era --color*/--borderRadius*/--elevation* aliases kept as a read-only compatibility layer whose values point at the same MD3 tokens.

The six MD3 shape tiers live as --md-shape-* (4dp/8dp/12dp/16dp/28dp/full in vw) and are registered into Tailwind borderRadius by top-level replacement so Tailwind's default rem tiers cannot leak in; 2xl/3xl are deliberately undefined, and a bare directional class such as rounded-t resolves to DEFAULT = medium (12dp), not extra-small.

The type scale is encoded as 15 semantic fontSize tiers, each an array of ['<size>', { lineHeight, letterSpacing }] with rpx = sp x 2, while weight is carried separately by extend.fontWeight (regular 400 / medium 500); tier names were kept stable so existing text-* class usage gained correct line heights without edits.

The ten legacy font-size aliases (xs/sm/base/lg/xl/2xl/3xl/4xl/5xl/6xl) each carry a full quadruple copied from their nearest MD3 tier but keep deliberately collapsed sizes (base/lg/xl all 28rpx, 5xl/6xl both 56rpx); the collapse and the compatibility role are intentional, and new code must use semantic tiers.

Body/label text must not add a self-chosen leading-* class: the tier already carries line height, and md3GuardScans rule 3 fails any class string that combines a font-size class with a leading-* utility, with only reasoned, per-form whitelist entries for arbitrary-size icon/decorative text.

700 weight is outside the registered MD3 weight scale and is machine-limited to a single documented brand wordmark (pages/Login.vue), whose whitelist entry must carry a marker string that actually exists in the source so the exemption cannot be silently erased.

State layers are four states x five roles = 20 translucent alpha tokens (hover .08 / focus .12 / pressed .12 / dragged .16) registered as top-level Tailwind colour keys so the utility names are bg-layer-<state>-<role>; registering them nested under state produces the differently named bg-state-layer-* classes, which are legacy aliases, and writing the wrong nesting yields a dead class name that silently produces no CSS.

The on-primary state layers are the one exception to alpha: because Lynx's background-color is a replacement rather than a composite, an alpha layer over a solid bg-primary erases the fill, so ADR-0207 decision 8 pre-computes them as opaque per-palette hex, closing the scope to that family while the other four roles must stay translucent, and constraining bg-layer-*-on-primary to elements that also carry bg-primary.

Pressed feedback may only use Tailwind active: variants: hover-class is banned outright because real-device probing showed it produces no visual change even for opaque positive controls, and the gate fails any .vue that binds hover-class regardless of the class value so that unrelated classes cannot slip past.

Disabled styling is a separate state, not a fifth alpha tier: --md-state-disabled-container (on-surface 12%) and --md-state-disabled-on-surface (38%) are defined and value-gated for every palette, but the disabled container must be its own overlay layer because placing it on the same element as a bg-surface-container-* class silently loses it to Tailwind declaration order, and consumption of these tokens is still incomplete with most components approximating disabled via opacity-40/50.

Hierarchy is expressed tone-first, shadow-second: each UI kind maps to a surface-container/or inverse-surface tone plus an allowed maximum shadow tier, surface-lying elements and skeletons take zero shadow achieved by deleting the shadow declaration (never by writing shadow-[var(--md-elevation-0)]), and active:shadow-[var(--md-elevation-*)] is banned because elevation is a height language rather than a state language.

Elevation levels 4 and 5 are extrapolated from a reproducible rule in tokens.css rather than taken from an upstream first-hand table, and they are kept defined but unconsumed; ADR-0212 records a criterion that they stay at zero consumers, and that criterion has no dedicated gate, so a hand-written level-4 shadow would only be caught by review.

--md-surface-tint takes the same value as that palette's --md-primary in all 14 palettes, so it has no intensity ladder and cannot express elevation; its role is narrowed to a state-layer-style overlay (the only consumer is PagePickerSheet.vue at 8%), and using bg-surface-tint on a card or sheet to imply elevation is a regression.

The icon pipeline has exactly one source: ICON_CODEPOINTS in src/utils/iconMap.ts is simultaneously the subset-font generator input, the runtime name-to-glyph lookup (iconChar throws on unregistered names instead of rendering blank) and the gate oracle, and components/AppIcon.vue is the only legal place a glyph is produced, taking name, label (forwarded to accessibility-label), size (default 6.4vw) and class.

The icon font must be the single generated, base64-inlined global @font-face in src/styles/icon-font.css: component-local @font-face declarations are forbidden because Lynx's url() only accepts remote addresses and base64, and the bundler-rewritten webpack:/// path silently fails on device so every icon would render as a tofu box with all gates green.

The bare-glyph gate (md3GuardScans rule 7) only covers specific Unicode ranges (arrows, geometric shapes, misc symbols, dingbats, misc arrows, emoji, private use, VS16), so the literal multiplication-sign close control still present in components/BottomSheet.vue is a residual that is not machine-guarded.

Icon inventory is conserved in both directions: the map must agree with the font subset's cmap and the official Material Symbols codepoints, and every registered name must have at least one real consumer in a file that renders AppIcon or mentions IconName, so entries with no consumer fail rather than silently wasting subset size.

Every production form input follows the M3 filled-text-field form as a statically checkable class contract (56dp tall, top 4dp shape token / bottom 0dp, bottom 1px on-surface-variant indicator), with the global search pill registered as the single exemption and a dead-registration rule that fails an exemption which no longer matches a real violation; the container colour surface-container-highest is required but deliberately not among the gate's asserted items.

Filled-text-field mechanics that generalise: the floating label is driven by Lynx bindfocus/bindblur element events rather than the unavailable :focus pseudo-class (two different mechanisms that must not be conflated), and the focused indicator is implemented as a separate overlay element rather than a mutually exclusive border class pair, because two declarations for the same property resolve by Tailwind's output order and the focused colour silently loses.

Geometry-sensitive Material components are consolidated rather than copy-pasted and each consolidation is held by a migration gate that fails if the inline markup returns: M3Switch (whose minimal { checked } interface with no emit and no a11y bindings is deliberate, to avoid double TalkBack announcements) and M3SegmentedButton are both guarded by callsite floors and by signature strings that may only appear in the component and its template test.

Theming is seven static accent palettes crossed with three dark-mode states, applied only as root page classes by appearanceClasses; the seven dark palettes are generated from the light --md-primary anchors through M3 SchemeTonalSpot with isDark=true (not inverted), the generated block in tokens.css is marked do-not-hand-edit, palettes-drift.test.ts locks generator output and anchors in both directions, and no palette value is ever computed at runtime.

Unit conversion is fixed by the 375pt design width: 1sp = 2rpx and 1dp = 0.2667vw, so fontSize is expressed in rpx while spacing and shape are expressed in vw; scaling with screen width instead of fixed dp/sp is a registered trade-off (proportions preserved), MD3's sp font-scaling semantics are absent by engine/unit limitation, and rem is banned from the config and the web-core preview path.

Intentional MD3 deviations are a closed list of five items (no dynamic colour, the 42px search pill, 48px secondary tabs, hover not applicable, focus/focus-visible not applicable); anything not on the list is treated as a defect by default, and re-opening an item requires a new ADR overturning ADR-0205 decision 4. The list is documented with exactly five rows in AGENTS.md, each citing an existing ADR, and a documentation gate enforces that.

The focus / focus-visible deviation is backed by a real-device probe with a positive control: :active changed pixels while both focus pseudo-classes changed nothing (engine does not match them), and :focus-visible additionally needs a keyboard/D-pad trigger the app does not have; writing either variant is a dead class name, the gate fails any bare :focus / focus-visible / focus: / focus-visible:, and accessibility is carried by accessibility-element plus the platform-drawn focus ring.

src/errorPrototype/ErrorPagePreview.vue is the one file-level exception named by the hardcode rule: it is not in router.ts and is reachable only through the dev web entry, its px hardcoding is deliberate, the no-hardcode clause does not cover it, it is registered in the whitelists, and it is explicitly not an example to copy; the documentation gate asserts both that it stays out of the production router and that the exception remains recorded.

Beyond that prototype page, the colour-hardcode gate scans src/**/*.{vue,ts} for hex, rgb()/rgba() and named colour utilities while permanently exempting tokens.css, and the remaining whitelist entries are semantic exceptions registered with reasons and, in several cases, explicit removal conditions (scrim-overlay white text, Lynx platform colour attributes, the immersive letterbox black), with a dead-entry ratchet so an exemption that stops matching a real violation turns the gate red.

Compliance claims require three layers of evidence (static audit, human-judged device screenshots, machine assertions on device), because Lynx's CSS is a subset in which a declaration existing in source does not prove it takes effect on device; a gap counts as closed only when the phenomenon is gone, machine-judgeable parts are asserted, and non-judgeable parts are screenshotted.

Every gate described on this page is a source/AST/contract gate that cannot observe rendering, so 'all gates green' means 'no known violation in the source' rather than 'the user-visible result is correct'; the repo has recorded cases (a :style binding rendered as literal page text, and an undefended full-page reflow on a system-bar toggle) that passed every static check.

Verification responsibility is split: md3ConfigTokens.test.ts answers only 'are the values in tailwind.config.ts and tokens.css the official ones', while md3GuardScans.test.ts answers 'has a violating form been written back into src/**', and mdTokenRefs.test.ts separately fails any var(--md-*) reference with no definition in tokens.css so mistyped token names cannot silently void a declaration.

The Fluent Design chapter is historical archive with no force for app-lynx, and the '### app-lynx 的 MD3 约定' section of AGENTS.md is the single current statement of design constraints: a documentation gate fails if a second current-constraint statement reappears, if Fluent-only token names or carriers leak outside the archive, or if the archive notice's links break.
